Review of `f8fcd55be77b0810e8556aa3f5b75550406756de` (cold tree checked out by sha; stacked on #773 → #771; its own delta is one file, `pr_mutations.rs` +27, and **zero test changes**).

**HOLD. B1 as written is fail-open, and R8's negative controls are absent.**
1. **Fail-open on an unreadable policy.** `if let Ok(mut approval_policy) = read_policy(…) && approval_policy.required { … }`: when the policy file cannot be read (rate limit, 404, auth), the whole gate is skipped and the enqueue proceeds. R1 says approval is a precondition; an unreadable policy must refuse with a reason, exactly as the `Err` arm of `evaluate_with_policy` already does.
2. **`&Value::Null` is passed as the queue observation.** `evaluate_with_policy(…, policy, queue)` takes the merge-queue/ejection record; passing `Null` disables whatever that argument gates (the ejection-after-approval check in `head_approval`). The steward has the live observation in `context.observation`; pass it.
3. **R1's record is not kept.** The approval comment id (or review id) is not written to the write-ahead intent or the receipt; `gate.explain()` text is returned only on refusal. R1: "The approval comment id goes into the write-ahead intent and the receipt."
4. **No tests, so no R8.** The ruling requires a replay negative where a `reviewed:` comment names an **earlier** head and must not arm, with the reason in the receipt, and break-confirm through the real steward entry point with a fake GitHub. None exist in this PR; `head_approval`'s own unit tests do not exercise the steward's enqueue path.
5. `approval_policy.required = true;` inside `if … && approval_policy.required` is a no-op; drop it.
6. Inherited own reds from #771/#773 (formatting on every leg, clippy), plus `pr_mutations.rs:105,123` formatting of its own.

reviewed: f8fcd55be77b0810e8556aa3f5b75550406756de fable-review-b (HOLD)

Review of head `cc491a1edbf40d622508d146c3a3a08943256265` (API-confirmed; cold worktree checked out by sha; the PR as opened carries #771 (D) and #773 (B4) underneath, its own B1 delta is `2abcab54..cc491a1e`). Judged against the Fable ruling R1/R8 in `goals/2026-10-11-shipyard-drives-every-pr-to-close.md`, with tests and mutants run on m1 (`cargo 1.97.1`, private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, a `Compiling shipyard` line observed on every build).

**Verdict: HOLD.** Two of the four prior must-fixes are fixed; two are still open, and R1 has three further gaps that each arm a head R1 says must not arm.

### Prior must-fixes
1. Fail-open on an unreadable policy: **fixed.** `read_policy` `Err` now returns `(None, Some("head approval policy unreadable: …"))` before any guard or mutation. Confirmed through the real `enqueue_pull_request` with a fake `gh` that 500s on `contents/.shipyard/config.toml`: no stack/enqueue call is made. Mutant M1 (`Err(_) => ApprovalPolicy::default()`, 16-line diff) is caught by that probe (ok -> FAILED) and **by nothing in the PR's own suite** (290 passed / 12 pre-existing auth-fixture failures, identical set before and after the mutant).
2. `Value::Null` as the queue observation: **fixed.** The live `PR_QUEUE_STATE_QUERY` is read per PR and a transport or JSON error fails closed.
3. Approval id in the intent and receipt: **still open.** `Ok(HeadGate::Approved { .. }) => {}` discards the approval; the write-ahead intent is still just the guard purpose string and no receipt or ledger audit carries a comment id. The new `comment_id` field is dead in production: `evaluate_with_policy` projects comments through `.[] | {login, type, at, body}` with no `id`, so `comment.get("id")` is always `None`; the new unit test feeds `"id": 4242` straight into `find_approval` and never crosses that jq.
4. Tests / R8 negatives: **still open.** The test delta is `wake_owner: false` and `author: None` field fills, two `classify_pr` tests (B4/A scope) and one `find_approval` unit test. Zero tests reach the gate through `enqueue_pull_request` / `mutate_pr_with_recovery`; no earlier-head replay negative exists. Mutants M2 (marker ignores the head) and M3 (bot/self identity no longer excluded) are caught only by `head_approval` unit tests, never by a steward entry-point test.
5. No-op `approval_policy.required = true`: fixed.

### R1 gaps found (each demonstrated through the real `enqueue_pull_request`, fake `gh`, policy `arm_requires_head_approval = true`, `reviewer_logins = ["reviewer"]`)
Probes held correctly for: marker naming an EARLIER head (`waiting_head_approval`, "carries no approval" in the error; the R8 negative), no comment at all, policy read error. Probes that **armed** (gate passed into stack discovery):
- **Later HOLD ignored.** `reviewed:<head>` by `reviewer`, then a later "HOLD. do not arm." by the same recognized reviewer: arms. A single comment "HOLD. must-fix list follows.\nreviewed:<head>" also arms. `find_approval` has no HOLD / CHANGES REQUESTED check at all, so the "drop the HOLD check" mutant is vacuous: there is nothing to drop.
- **Author may approve own head.** `StewardPullRequest.author` is added but never consulted by the gate; PR author `reviewer` approved by `reviewer` arms.
- **Absent policy arms unapproved heads.** 404 on `.shipyard/config.toml` -> `ApprovalPolicy::default()` -> `NotRequired` -> arm. Shipyard's own `main` has no `[auto_merge]` table, so the live steward on this repo would arm every green fleet head with no approval. R1 makes approval the precondition of the enqueue class; opt-in cannot be the steward's default.
- **7-hex prefix accepted** (`reviewed:aaaaaaa` arms). R1 says `reviewed:<40-hex>`; `carrier.rs:481` already requires 40.

### Must-fix before this head can be approved
1. Carry the `Approval` out of the gate; add `id: .id` to the comments jq; write `approval_comment_id` (or review id) and the reviewer login into the write-ahead intent and the enqueue receipt / ledger audit. Test through `enqueue_pull_request` that the id appears in the persisted record.
2. Refuse when any later comment by a recognized reviewer (or a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review) says HOLD / CHANGES REQUESTED for this head or newer, and when the approving comment itself says HOLD. Tests for both.
3. Reject an approval whose login equals the PR author (pass `author` into `decide` / `find_approval`). Test.
4. In the steward enqueue path, treat `!policy.required` (including the 404 default) as a refusal with a reason, not `NotRequired`; the opt-in semantics may stay for `shipyard pr --arm` and the native-arm backstop. Test with a 404 config.
5. Add the entry-point probe set in `merge_steward_cmd/tests` (positive with id in receipt; earlier head; missing; policy error; later HOLD; self-approval; absent policy), each break-confirmed. The fail-open mutant surviving the entire suite is the proof this is needed.

Should-fix: pin one marker grammar and use it in both `head_approval` and the carrier (40-hex; decide whether a single space after the colon is allowed, since every fleet reviewer comment so far, including the HOLD above, writes `reviewed: <sha>` and would never match the current `^\s*reviewed:[0-9a-f]{7,40}\s*$`); check the comment is newer than the head commit (`newer_than` is `None` outside the ejection-cap path).

### CI on this head
Not green on the required leg. CI run 38132409880 `macOS ARM64 [local]` (Shipyard-studio-02): "Run tests" cancelled at 10:57Z after 23 min, job `failure`, log blob already 404 so the cause cannot be read. Sandbox E2E run 38132412992 `macOS ARM64 [local]`: queued since 10:34Z with no runner. Linux, Windows, Coverage, Python helper tests, Versioning & Skill-Sync: success.

Verdict: HOLD at head cc491a1edbf40d622508d146c3a3a08943256265 (fable-review-c). Not an approval; no `reviewed:` marker is issued for this head.

Review of `07b1a624254c0e257f088909b2f79f429769ee0d` (cold tree checked out by sha; stacked on #771 at 2fd82280, so it inherits #771's holds; its own delta is 6 files, +77).

**HOLD.**
1. **One comment per state change (R6) is not enforced.** `wake_owner_comment` is called whenever `args.wake_owner && decision ∈ {NeedsUpdate, RequiredFailed}` on an apply pass. There is no transition check and no record of a prior wake, so a PR that stays `NeedsUpdate` gets a new comment every pass. The docstring says "Callers gate this behind a state transition"; no caller does.
2. **The owner is not woken.** R7 defines owner = whence session, else last committer, else team-lead, and #771 now computes exactly that in `owner_for`. The comment body is `Shipyard owner wake: PR #N at exact head … requires action: …` with no owner named, mentioned, or messaged; the inbox/handback path that reaches a session is not used. This is a generic comment, not an owner wake.
3. **No test exercises the wake.** The only test-file change is `wake_owner: false` added to five fixtures. Needed: one wake per transition (pass twice, one comment), no wake when the decision is unchanged, no wake without `--wake-owner`, the exact-head re-verification refusing when the head moved, and the owner derivation.
4. `mutation_context.as_ref().expect("apply mode requires mutation control")` is a panic path in production; return the error.
5. Own CI red: `Check formatting` on every leg (inherited #771 diffs plus `cancellation.rs:334`); clippy `this function has too many lines (117/100)` at `cancellation.rs:248` (own). On m1, 12 tests in `handoff::`, `recovery_worker::github::` and `stale_pr_wedge::` fail with my broader filter; those need a gh/git environment and CI stopped at formatting before running tests, so I could not control them; fix formatting and let CI say.

reviewed: 07b1a624254c0e257f088909b2f79f429769ee0d fable-review-b (HOLD)

Review of `ee8d223b9ff4c7de4db066a57bba8bfa08f728f3` (sy-review-773; cold worktree checked out by sha; API head matched before and after; mutants built and run on m1 with a dedicated target dir, one `Compiling shipyard` line and a non-empty diff asserted per mutant).

**Fixed since the prior HOLD:** the `.expect()` panic path on the wake is gone (returns `owner wake requires mutation control`); `fmt`/`clippy` are green; all 10 check runs on this head are `success` (Linux, macOS ARM64 [local], Windows, Coverage, Python helpers, version & skill sync).

**HOLD.** Must-fix:

1. **The wake still does not name the owner (R7).** `owner_wake_body` uses `pr.fact.author`. The steward observes `author` via `gh pr list --json ... author`, and gh renders the fleet App as `app/shipyard-local` (measured in this repo just now: `ghapp pr list --state all --limit 6 --json number,author` prints `app/shipyard-local is_bot=true` for #767-#774). So every fleet PR would be woken "for app/shipyard-local". R7 is whence session, else last committer, else team-lead, and this PR already ships exactly that as `owner_for` in `src/app/pr_status_cmd.rs:191`; wire the wake to it (the `repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}` read in `verify_exact_open_pr` already returns `body`; read `/commits` for the last committer) and add a test whose fixture author is `app/shipyard-local` with a whence block in the body, asserting the session is named and the bot login is not. Note (from the #771 review, https://github.com/danielraffel/Shipyard/pull/771#issuecomment-6110618238): `owner_for` itself reads `commits.nodes[].commit.author.login`, but gh emits a flat `commits[].authors[].login`, so wired as-is it names `team-lead` for every PR without a whence block; fix the shape there (or read it from the REST `/commits` response) before wiring the wake to it, and have the test feed gh's real shape.

2. **No test through the real steward apply entry point.** The only new tests are unit tests of `should_wake_owner` and `owner_wake_body`; `tests/mutations.rs` only gained `wake_owner: false` on five fixtures and no test sets `wake_owner: true`. Mutants on m1 (filter `merge_steward`, baseline 271 pass / 12 env-only failures in `handoff::`, `recovery_worker::github::`, `stale_pr_wedge::`, identical on every run):
   - M1 remove `&& !signal_is_converged(pr, true)` from `should_wake_owner`: killed only by `recovery::tests::owner_wake_only_occurs_on_transition_into_needs_agent`.
   - M2 drop `{owner}` from the body: killed only by `recovery::tests::owner_wake_body_names_the_owner`.
   - M3 drop `args.wake_owner &&` in `apply_pr_plans` (wake fires without the flag): **SURVIVES**.
   - M4 delete the `verify_exact_open_pr` call before the POST: **SURVIVES**.
   Needed, through `apply_pr_plans`/`steward_command` with the fake gh: pass twice on an unchanged `RequiredFailed` head produces exactly one `issues/{n}/comments` POST; no `--wake-owner` produces zero; head moved between observe and post produces zero plus an error; owner derivation per item 1.

3. **The "transition" is another write's convergence, read from the stale snapshot.** `should_wake_owner` is `!signal_is_converged(pr, true)` on the pre-mutation observation, i.e. "the needs-agent label + FAILURE status are not yet on this head". Two consequences: (a) `reconcile_recovery_signal` revalidates against the live PR and skips when live is already converged, but the wake keys on `pr` (observed), so a stale observation posts a repeat comment with no transition (R6); (b) any `--apply` pass without `--wake-owner`, or a crash after the label write and before the comment POST, converges the signal, and the owner is then never woken for that head. The wake needs its own dedupe record (ledger entry keyed repo/pr/head, or a live check for its own exact-head marker comment) and, per R4 row 15, a write-ahead intent like the handoff path has (`intent_is_durable_before_the_first_github_mutation`); add the crash-between-writes test.

4. **No escalation exists.** R7: after 2 h STALLED, once to the owner, then to team-lead. The PR has no escalation path (grep of the delta for escalat/STALLED in the wake finds nothing), so the "allow repeat escalation" mutant has no target. Either implement it against the ledger's STALLED computation, or state explicitly in the PR that B4 lands without escalation and record the follow-up in planning.

5. **Stacking is stale.** This head carries #771 at `2fd82280`; #771's head is now `5913e6f1`, which adds back `pr.author.is_some()` in `classify_management` and the daemon fleet-repo test, and `git merge-tree --write-tree ee8d223b 5913e6f1` conflicts in `src/merge_steward/tests.rs`. It merges clean on `main` today only because #771 is unmerged (merge-base == origin/main). Rebase onto #771's current head or land after it and merge main.

6. **Inherited from #771 but load-bearing here:** `fleet_author` matches `shipyard-local[bot]`, which gh never emits (see item 1), and `human_or_dependabot` (`!author.ends_with("[bot]")`) is therefore TRUE for App PRs, so a fleet-branch PR opened by the App classifies as human and stays `Unmanaged`, never reaching `NeedsUpdate`/`RequiredFailed`, never woken. Reported to #771's reviewer; this PR should add one entry-point test using the real `app/shipyard-local` login so B4 is proven on a fleet PR as observed.

Should-fix: `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` on `apply_pr_plans` suppresses the lint the prior review flagged rather than extracting the wake block; `--wake-owner` without `--apply` is a silent no-op (the wake sits inside `if args.apply`), so the CLI should reject or warn.

Verdict for ee8d223b9ff4c7de4db066a57bba8bfa08f728f3: HOLD

comments.body:
Review of `1cf21af8a53229e4f46c1b46b14d4b9218f45ee3` (cold detached tree checked out by sha; base main 83f0df29; 4 files; CI green on every finished leg, macOS local still running).

**The choke point works with the real guard.** I pointed `scripts/gh` at the repo's actual `ghapp_queue_removal_guard.py` (not the test's fake) and drove it with the forms an agent types:

```
rc=1  api graphql -f   query=mutation{disablePullRequestAutoMerge(...)}   refusing unaudited merge-queue removal
rc=1  api graphql -f   query=mutation { dequeuePullRequest(...) }         refused
rc=1  api graphql -F   query=mutation{dequeuePullRequest(...)}            refused
rc=1  api graphql --raw-field query=mutation{disablePullRequestAutoMerge} refused
rc=1  api graphql --input body.json  (mutation inside the JSON body)      refused
rc=1  pr merge --disable-auto 123                                          refused
rc=0  pr view 1                                                            native gh ran
```

So the Codex-01a126a2 bypass (`gh api graphql disablePullRequestAutoMerge`) is closed once this file sits ahead of native `gh` on PATH, and the native binary is never reached on a refusal.

**HOLD on three deploy defects, each small.**
1. **It refuses to run at all when `SHIPYARD_GHAPP_GUARDS_DIR` is unset**, even though the guards live at the default `ghapp` uses (`${SHIPYARD_GHAPP_GUARDS_DIR:-$HOME/.config/shipyard/guards}`, present on this host). Installed ahead of `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`, every `gh` call from a launchd agent, cmux pane or Codex session without that export prints "queue-removal guard is unavailable; refusing to run" and exits 1. Resolve the guard the way `ghapp` does; fail closed only when the resolved guard is genuinely missing.
2. **The test proves the wrapper's plumbing, not the guard.** `test_plain_gh_guard.py` installs a fake `queue-removal-guard` that greps `$*`, so a guard that stopped parsing `-f query=` would still pass it. Point the test at the real `scripts/ghapp_queue_removal_guard.py` (a two-line shim, as above) and assert one refusal per form: `-f`, `-F`, `--raw-field`, `--input`, `pr merge --disable-auto`, plus the harmless pass-through.
3. **Nothing installs it.** There is no install step, no PATH placement, and the only doc change is the wait-guidance section; the deliverable says "a shell hook or wrapper on the same choke point as ghapp", which is a host change this PR does not describe. Add the placement to the ci skill (where it goes, how `SHIPYARD_NATIVE_GH_BINARY` is set when Homebrew is elsewhere) and, if the fleet installer owns PATH, the install step.

Nits: `test_plain_gh_guard.py` is a module-level script with `assert`s, so under `unittest discover` it runs at import and reports as a collection error rather than a test case; a `unittest.TestCase` would be clearer. The bounded-wait section in `skills/ci/SKILL.md` is right (`pgrep -f '[g]ates.sh'`, a deadline, `shipyard wait … --timeout`), and its text test pins it.

comments.body:
Review of `c379a4c673e583a60dc14b2fecb70f884e80fa11` (cold detached tree checked out by sha; base main 83f0df29; no conflicts; on m1: fmt clean, clippy clean apart from the toolchain-drift `Duration` lint main also trips, `merge_steward:: app::pr_status_cmd:: app::daemon_cmd::` 53 passed; CI Linux/Coverage/Python green, macOS and Windows still running. The "auth-fixture failures" ws19 saw are the known linked-worktree fake-gh effect and the clippy lints are the m1 toolchain drift; CI is the control and it is green on the legs that have finished, so neither is this PR's.)

**HOLD. Three of the four features ship without a test, and the management rule does not match R5.**

Mutants against the full three modules:
- Killed: S1 remove the fleet-branch default → `fleet_branch_is_managed_by_default_and_opt_out_still_wins` FAILS.
- **Survive, 53 OK each:** S2 drop `feature/` and `fix/` from the prefix list; S3 remove the daemon's default repo list (`daemon start` with no repos watches nothing again); S4 drop the 2 h threshold so every non-queue-ready PR is STALLED. `pr_status_cmd.rs` (174 lines) has no test at all, nor does the daemon default, nor the `action` positional.

**R5 is not what was implemented.** The ruling: "managed = authored by the fleet App or from a codex/*, feature/*, fix/* branch, minus the opt-out label. Human-authored and Dependabot PRs stay Unmanaged unless opted in." The code manages by branch prefix alone; `StewardPullRequest` carries no author, so a human's `fix/typo` or `feature/x` branch becomes managed, and a fleet-App-authored PR on any other branch name stays Unmanaged. Dependabot stays Unmanaged only because its branches are `dependabot/…`. Add the author to the model and require fleet App authorship (or a configured agent-author list) for the prefix rule, with tests: human `fix/` → Unmanaged, App-authored non-prefixed → managed, Dependabot → Unmanaged.

**R7 is not what was implemented.** STALLED is defined as no head movement, no comment and no check-state change for 2 h on a PR that is not queue-ready; the ledger uses `updatedAt` age, which does not move on check-state changes, so a PR whose required run has been in progress for two hours reads STALLED. Owner is defined as the whence-provenance session, else the branch's last committer, else team-lead; the ledger prints the GitHub author login (which is `shipyard-local[bot]` for most fleet PRs) and falls back to team-lead only when the field is missing. `next_action` is a fixed `observe`/`owner-wake` string. These are the D slice's whole content; they need the R7 definitions and tests for each (a check-state change within 2 h is not stalled; whence block parsed; committer fallback).

**Smaller, same PR.**
- The ledger shells out to plain `gh pr list`, not the App-authenticated `ghapp` every other Shipyard GitHub read uses; on a fleet host that is the wrong identity (and after #772 it routes through the guard for nothing).
- `shipyard pr <ACTION>` accepts any positional and silently ignores everything but `status`; `shipyard pr typo` would ship a PR. Make it an enum or error on unknown values.
- The three-repo list is copied three times (`daemon_start`, `daemon_run`, `configured_repositories`); one constant.

What is right: read-only is real (no mutation path in `pr_status_cmd`), the opt-out label is checked before management so it wins (S1's test proves the precedence), and the CLI/daemon plumbing compiles and passes the existing suites.

reviewed: c379a4c673e583a60dc14b2fecb70f884e80fa11 fable-review-b (HOLD)

Review of `2fd822801e5a076429c3aeace44c2174e3f179e3` (cold tree checked out by sha; on m1 `merge_steward:: app::pr_status_cmd:: app::daemon_cmd:: app::cli::` 83 passed).

**Fixed since c379a4c6.** R5 is author-aware: `fleet_author || (fleet_branch && !human_or_dependabot)`, pinned by `fleet_management_uses_author_and_branch_quadrants` (my S6, letting a human's `fix/` branch through, FAILS it). R7 movement is the max of `updatedAt`, commit dates, comment times and check `completedAt` (S7, ignoring check completion, FAILS `stalled_uses_latest_of_head_comment_and_check_movement`). Owner prefers the whence session. The ledger reads through `ghapp`. `shipyard pr <ACTION>` rejects anything but `status` and `--all` without it. One `FLEET_REPOSITORIES` constant.

**HOLD on what remains.**
1. **Own CI red on every leg.** `Check formatting` fails on `carrier/tests.rs`, `recovery.rs`, `tests/admission.rs`, `tests/observation.rs`, `pr_status_cmd.rs` (the PR touched all five without `cargo fmt`), and clippy under `-D warnings`: `items after a test module` at `pr_status_cmd.rs:180` (the two helper fns sit below `mod tests`).
2. **Two mutants still survive.** S2 drop `feature/` and `fix/` from the prefix list → 83 passed (the quadrants test uses `codex/` only). S4 drop the 2 h threshold so every non-queue-ready PR is STALLED → 83 passed (`stalled_uses_latest_…` checks the movement timestamp, not the threshold). One assertion each. (My S3 on the daemon default did not compile as written, so it is inconclusive; I found no test naming `FLEET_REPOSITORIES` in `daemon_cmd.rs` either.)
3. **Owner falls back to the *first* committer, not the last.** `owner_for` reads `/commits/nodes/0/commit/author/login`; `gh pr list --json commits` lists oldest first, and R7 says "the branch's last committer". Use the last node. The owner test has one commit, so it cannot see this.

## fable-graph design ruling on the same-base keyed canary (for 30558de0 and its successor)

**Ruling: ADOPT fable-review-b's shape.** Both passes run inside Shipyard's own execution loop, never inside one shell string, because the executable-reuse binding is a planner OUTPUT: it can only bind to pass 1's record if the planner runs after pass 1. No smaller shape is same-base by construction. The one smaller shape I considered, copying pass 1's record into the binding file before pass 2 within the shell command, still leaves the planner's choice unexercised and proves `bind_keyed_pass` only on a hand-fed record, which the pure-function unit tests already prove. Rejected.

The shape, with amendments that make the receipt honest:

1. **Pass 1** = the existing `shadow_compare` lane with `COMPARE_FULL=1`, publishing its record to the host store (`reuse_record = true`, `SHIPYARD_REUSE_RECORD_DIR`). Pass 1 is where false_skips is computed, so **fact 6 (false_skips == 0) and fact 5 (would_skip > 0 for the shadow derivation) are read from pass 1's shadow comparison**, never from pass 2.
2. **Ingest, then RE-PLAN keyed** pinned to pass 1's recorded `base_sha` and tree sha, on the SAME checkout. The planner sees the full host store; the restriction is enforced by **`bind_keyed_pass(pass1_record, planner_choice)` called on the planner's real choice**, which refuses any record whose id is not pass 1's. A planner that chooses another record yields INCONCLUSIVE with a reason naming both ids. This is the contract mutant C1 must kill; a self-comparison `bind(record, record.clone())` is not an implementation of it.
3. **StaleBase in canary mode**: if main moved during pass 1, the re-plan records `StaleBase` as a fact and continues, because the canary's output is advisory and never a merge verdict. The authority path's refusal is untouched. Do not try to win the race with timing.
4. **Pass 2** runs `COMPARE_FULL=0` on the written binding; facts 3 (derived.status), 7 (rederivation match) and **8 (`selected_returncode == lane rc`, not full rc vs keyed rc) are read from pass 2**. **Any absent field is INCONCLUSIVE, never equal**; fact 8's current default-to-equal is fail-open and must go.
5. **The receipt is written on every exit path with a stated reason.** `test -s record || exit 75` before the writer is a defect: "pass 1 published no record" is a receipt, not an exit code. Same for planner refusal, StaleBase, and binding refusal.
6. **Tests drive `apply_changed_surface_execution` with fake lane commands**: (a) emits a record -> bound, PASS reachable with fake facts; (b) emits a different record id -> INCONCLUSIVE naming both ids (kills C1); (c) emits no record -> INCONCLUSIVE "no record" (kills C2); (d) `selected_returncode` absent -> fact 8 inconclusive (kills the fail-open default). Plus the `must_use` clippy item.

PASS requires all nine facts true from the sources above; FAIL on any false_skip, rederivation mismatch, fallback file, or binding refusal; INCONCLUSIVE when a fact's source is absent, with the reason in the receipt. Until this shape lands, no more canary lanes on pulp#10049; the two INCONCLUSIVE runs so far are the evidence that the lane-string shape cannot work, not noise to retry.

## fable-graph ruling for 74f00017 and its successor: the simplest same-base shape, and what to cut

**Answer to item 5 (which pass the facts come from): all of facts 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 come from PASS 2, and pass 2 runs in `shadow_compare` mode (`COMPARE_FULL=1`) bound to pass 1's record.** Pass 1 exists only to publish the record (`reuse_record = true`); none of its facts enter the receipt. Reasoning: pass 1's own keyed shadow can only bind to the planner's original record, so its would_skip/false_skips are not same-base by definition. false_skips needs a full result set to compare the keyed selection against; the only way to get a same-base false_skips without teaching Shipyard to intersect junit files is to let Pulp compute it the way it already does, inside one run that is both full and keyed-shadow, bound to pass 1's record. That is pass 2 in shadow_compare mode. Cost: two full runs per canary. Accepted: the canary is dispatch-only and exists to prove a property, not to be fast.

The receipt's nine facts then read from exactly two sources: the binding decision (Rust, from `bind_keyed_pass(pass1_record, planner_choice)`) for facts 1 and 2, and pass 2's `latest_result(result_dir)` for facts 3 to 9 (`derived.status`, audit staged->applied, `would_skip_count > 0`, `false_skip_count == 0`, rederivation match, `selected_returncode == lane rc`, no fallback file). Absent field = INCONCLUSIVE with the field named; never a default.

**The shape (sequence, one function, one writer):**
1. Pass 1: run `stages.test` with `SHIPYARD_CHANGED_SURFACE_RESULT_DIR=pass1_dir`, `reuse_record = true`, no binding file, no COMPARE_FULL. Outcome used: did it exit 0 and publish a record. Nothing else.
2. Ingest pass 1's record. Re-plan keyed, pinned to pass 1's base and tree on the same checkout; StaleBase is recorded as a fact and the canary continues (advisory).
3. `bind_keyed_pass(pass1_record, planner_choice)`; refused -> receipt INCONCLUSIVE naming both ids, stop.
4. Write `executable-reuse-binding.json` for the bound record into `pass2_dir` BEFORE pass 2 runs. This is the only ordering constraint in the design, and it is the one 74f00017 gets wrong (the binding is written after the branch that needs it).
5. Pass 2: run `stages.test` with `SHIPYARD_CHANGED_SURFACE_RESULT_DIR=pass2_dir`, `COMPARE_FULL=1`.
6. `persist_same_base_canary_receipt` in Rust, once, on every branch (success and all refusals), from the binding decision and `latest_result(pass2_dir)`. The lane command carries no Python.

**Cut from 74f00017:**
- `same_base_keyed_command`'s Python heredoc and the shell-built receipt: delete. One writer, Rust, after the lane returns.
- Every read of pass 1's `result-*.json` for facts: delete. Pass 1 contributes only "exited 0" and the record.
- `production_canary_mutants_are_break_confirmed` (the `include_str!` source grep): delete. A test that reads its own source is not a break-confirm.
- `t1..t4` as helper-level tests may stay as unit tests, but they do not count toward acceptance.

**Tests that count (each through `apply_changed_surface_execution` with `mode = same_base_canary` and a fake `stages.test` script):**
- (a) pass 1 writes a record; planner candidate is that record; pass 2 writes a result with all facts true -> PASS, binding written before pass 2 ran (assert the file's mtime or a marker the fake script reads).
- (b) planner candidate is a different record id -> INCONCLUSIVE, reason names both ids, pass 2 never runs.
- (c) pass 1 writes no record -> INCONCLUSIVE "pass 1 published no record", never PASS.
- (d) pass 1 exits non-zero -> INCONCLUSIVE, pass 2 never runs.
- (e) pass 2 result lacks `selected_returncode` (or `false_skip_count`) -> INCONCLUSIVE naming the field.
Then the two behavioural mutants fable-review-b wrote must fail: Z1 (candidate rebuilt from pass 1 -> self-bind) fails (b); Z2 (`if !pass1_succeeded` -> `if false`) fails (d). Run them and paste the failing assertion in the PR.

PASS requires all nine facts; FAIL on any false_skip, rederivation mismatch, fallback file, or binding refusal with a bound record; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, always with a reason. Smaller and correct beats another cycle: ship exactly this.
